newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank says constitution needs changes for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank says constitution needs changes for EMU.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Monday the bank's independence should be written into the nation's constitution to satisfy membership criteria for Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
The constitution should also be amended so that the grounds for dismissal of the bank's governor are specified and also applicable to other board members.
The Riksbank said in a statement that this was the opinion in a submission from the bank's governing board to the Finance Ministry.

In an analysis last September the under-secretaries for legal affairs in the Cabinet Office, the Justice Ministry and the Finance Ministry considered the extent the constitution needed to be amended if Sweden joined EMU.
"The governing board accordingly supports the assessment presented," the Riksbank said.

"Moreover the board supports the proposal in the memorandum that the constitution also be amended by including in the Constitution Act a provision to the effect that the Riksbank is independent of the Riksdag (parliament) and the government.
"The provision should amount to a ban on instructions to the Riksbank except in a statutory form."
